questions.q: By default, which direction does an RLS filter flow across a relationship?
options: Single-directional only, regardless of whether the relationship itself is set to bidirectional filtering
Always bidirectional, with no way to change it
It flows in a random direction determined at refresh time
RLS filters never cross any relationship at all
questions.explain: RLS filtering defaults to single-directional even on a relationship configured for bidirectional cross-filtering — reaching both directions requires an explicit opt-in.

questions.q: How do you enable bidirectional security filtering for a relationship?
options: Select the relationship in model view and check 'Apply security filter in both directions'
It's enabled automatically whenever dynamic RLS is used
Through a setting in the Power BI service only, never Desktop
By renaming the relationship
questions.explain: That specific checkbox on the relationship itself is the only way to turn on bidirectional security filtering.

questions.q: If a table participates in multiple bidirectional relationships, how many of them can have security filtering enabled in both directions?
options: Only one
All of them simultaneously
None — the feature is disabled entirely in that case
Exactly two
questions.explain: This is an explicit constraint: a table in multiple bidirectional relationships can only have the security-filter-both-directions option enabled on one of them.

questions.q: What is the main risk of enabling bidirectional security filtering broadly?
options: It can meaningfully hurt query performance, especially in large or highly-related models — it should be tested thoroughly and used deliberately
It makes RLS stop working entirely
It automatically disables all DAX measures in the model
There is no performance impact of any kind
questions.explain: The official guidance is explicit: this setting can negatively impact query performance, particularly in models with many relationships or large datasets — always test before deploying it.

questions.q: What can happen when USERELATIONSHIP() is used in a measure on a model that has RLS enabled?
options: It can cause unexpected errors — the fix is to redesign the DAX around model-level relationships rather than disabling RLS
USERELATIONSHIP() and RLS always work together with no issues
RLS automatically disables itself whenever USERELATIONSHIP() is used
USERELATIONSHIP() is required for RLS to function at all
questions.explain: RLS enabled alongside USERELATIONSHIP() in DAX queries and measures can produce unexpected errors — the documented workaround is redesigning around model-level relationships instead.
